title: DC-area forecast: A blissful start to the week before humidity, rain chances return
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Temperatures fall into and through the comfortable 70s this evening as bubbly clouds of the day dissipate.

What’s next? Tomorrow is much like today before it turns a little toastier Wednesday. Higher humidity and the chance of showers and storms return Thursday and Friday.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Mostly clear and pleasant. Evening temperatures quickly slip into the 70s, with overnight lows ranging from the mid-50s in our cooler spots to the mid-60s downtown. Confidence: High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Tuesday): It's more or less a carbon copy of Monday. Expect partly to mostly sunny skies and highs from 80 to 85. Light winds from the northwest. Confidence: High 😎 Nice Day!

Tomorrow night: Another mostly clear and comfortable evening and overnight. Lows are a few degrees warmer, ranging from the upper 50s to the mid- to upper 60s. Confidence: High

📬 Get our forecast in your inbox

Our morning forecast email is back! It's included with every level of support — from Free to Sustainer — delivered 7 days a week. Sign up at: capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

Sunny skies continue Wednesday, but it starts to feel somewhat steamy again. Highs reach 85 to 90 while dew points climb into the 60s. Partly cloudy at night with a slight chance of a shower or storm as more humid air oozes northward. Lows range from the 60s to near 70. Confidence: Medium-High

Thursday and Friday bring a return to the very warm and humid weather we've become accustomed to this month. Highs both days range from 85 to 90, and it feels like the 90s with dew points near and above 70. Showers and thunderstorms — mostly late in the day — are possible both days, but most likely Thursday. Overnight lows are near 70. Confidence: Medium-High

Somewhat less humid air arrives over the weekend, but a hint of mugginess may linger. Rain chances drop, and partly to mostly sunny skies may rule. Highs both days are mostly in the mid-80s, with nighttime lows in the 60s. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for August 24

A soaking 1967 storm dropped record rainfall, contributing to one of the wetter Augusts on record.

Today’s daily digit — 9/10: A top-tier late-summer day. Enjoy! | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
